Chapter 4: Taking Action and Embracing Change
So, now that you’ve got a clearer sense of your values—and you’re building that network of support around you—what’s next?
Here’s where a lot of people get stuck: moving from thinking and reflecting, to actually doing something about it.
Have you ever felt paralyzed by the fear of making the wrong choice? You’re definitely not alone. The truth is, the only real way to learn is by taking action—by actually doing.
Let me share a story. There was someone who spent months going back and forth, unsure what to do. Finally, she decided to apply for a job that, on paper, wasn’t a perfect fit. The interview process? Completely nerve-wracking. And when the offer came, she was hit with a mix of excitement and doubt. She accepted it, reminding herself, “Hey, this doesn’t have to be forever.”
Those first few weeks? Tough. Everything felt new—routines, tasks, even the people. She worried she just wouldn’t measure up. But as time passed, she found her rhythm. Sure, the job wasn’t quite what she’d pictured, but it ended up teaching her skills she never expected to learn.
Then there’s another example: someone who’d been freelancing and feeling a bit lost. Instead of waiting for the perfect plan, he set a new goal—to learn a new skill every month. He dove into online courses, tried workshops, practiced with small projects. Some skills stuck, others didn’t. But you know what? The process itself built his confidence and opened up doors he hadn’t even considered. He saw firsthand that being adaptable mattered more than sticking to a rigid plan.
Change is almost never comfortable. Often, it means letting go of old versions of yourself and stepping into something new. Think about a recent graduate who always saw herself as an academic. Her first job ended up being in a completely different field. At first, she felt like she was leaving a part of herself behind. But as she settled in, she discovered strengths she never knew she had—the experience actually broadened her vision of what was possible.
Most of us don’t even realize how much we grow by taking small risks. Signing up for a class, starting a tiny side project, or just reaching out to someone you admire—these steps build momentum. The future is shaped by what you do, not just what you plan. And yes, mistakes will happen. But honestly? Those are some of the best teachers you’ll ever have.
Embracing change means accepting that your path will have twists and turns. Careers are almost never straight lines. You’ll hit setbacks, you’ll take detours, and you’ll have moments where you doubt yourself. But every experience adds something valuable to your toolkit. Over time, you’ll notice your resilience growing. That fear of the unknown? It’ll start to fade, replaced by a sense of possibility.
The stories of people who took action—even when they weren’t completely sure—prove something powerful: progress comes from movement. If you wait for perfect clarity, you’ll never get started. The future? It’s built step by step, choice by choice. The most important thing you can do is simply to begin.
